audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] calls Nether Grasp 'QSS-proof' and tells the player to hold Cleanse for it — both backwards. QSS removes suppression; Cleanse does not. Also Void Shift (his passive CC immunity) is never mentioned, yet it eats Syndra's E stun unless popped first.
audit.why: Suppression is removed by QSS/Mercurial, not Cleanse; Malzahar passive grants CC immunity until damaged.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Check it before every step-up. - E Scatter the Weak is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp is 140/110/80s and point-and-click — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up; check it before every step forward. - His Q silence cycles every 6s; your E Scatter the Weak (15s) is the lifeline — chip damage never gets it. - Your R answers fights, not waves.

edits.before: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Your Q also pops Void Shift — his passive damage reduction and CC immunity. Poke first, stun second: an unpopped shield eats your E stun.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, W-slow the dodge attempt, QE the slowed line, Q again — a full bar of damage that started as routine poke.
edits.after: Two grounded spheres turn E into a near point-and-click stun and feed R's burst — the bank converts poke range into kill threat.

edits.before: Spending E on chip-spacing and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive unanswered — the stun is the matchup, not the damage.
edits.after: Immobile with E on a 15-second cooldown, you are the easiest suppress target in mid — his R plus a gank ends you before help arrives.

edits.before: Malzahar gets a QSS-proof suppress and a strong DoT teamfight, so respect his R in skirmishes, but you still win the sidelane and pick game. Buy or hold cleanse timing for his ult, focus him from range with R burst, and never let him land the full silence-suppress chain. Your one-shot from distance beats his channel.
edits.after: Malzahar's Nether Grasp is a suppression — Cleanse does not remove it, but QSS does, and any CC on him breaks the channel. Respect his R in skirmishes, but you still win the sidelane and pick game: focus him from range with R burst and never let the silence-suppress chain start. Your one-shot from distance beats his channel.
